speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo. To help me pinpoint the cause, can you describe exactly what the sensation feels like—is it a spinning motion or just a feeling of unsteadiness?

Also, how long does an episode typically last, and did it start immediately upon waking or during a specific activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor

Thank you for that detailed description. Since the spinning sensation lasted only 3 minutes, was it triggered specifically by head movements like turning your head in bed or looking up? Additionally, do you notice any other symptoms such as double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your arms or legs?
